Definition: a prolonged form of a primary verb, δόκω (used only in an alternate in certain tenses; compare the base of G1166) of the same meaning; to think; by implication, to seem (truthfully or uncertainly):--be accounted, (of own) please(-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow.
BiblicalUsage: To think, to seem, what a person supposes, whether it is true or not. Paul warns that if anyone thinks he is wise in this world, he must become a fool to become wise, and Peter did not think the angel's rescue was real. Paul laid his gospel before the leaders at Jerusalem in case he had run in vain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe thinking and knowing are not the same thing, and my opinions need the same testing Paul gave his own gospel. What seems wise to me may be foolishness to God, and I would rather find that out in His word than at the end of my life.
